traits.leader.note: iNaturalist research-grade photographs (observations 18299511, 185799293, 37979372, 142536045): a few thick limbs spread from the top of the swollen trunk.

traits.bark_colour.note: The bark colour chosen by eye for appearance (see its note), as a screen colour: it stood as appearance.bark [0.55, 0.5, 0.45], which is linear light, so the trunk drew pale grey to white beside photographs of the species (2026-10-23). It stands here in sRGB, as bark colours are picked, and the bark rule (tracheophyta) turns it into linear light.

traits.leaf_out_months.note: Wikipedia, Adansonia digitata (read 2026-10-18): "All baobabs are deciduous, losing their leaves in the dry season, and remaining leafless for about eight months of the year." Its leaves come with the southern African summer rains; December is ours.

traits.leaf_fall_months.note: Wikipedia, Adansonia digitata (read 2026-10-18): leafless "for about eight months of the year" in the dry season: shed in March and April, ours, so it stands in leaf about four months.

generator.params.bole_clear.note: The trunk stands bare to the fork about 8 m up (crown_base 8, was 7; crown_height 13, was 12), where five or so thick limbs spread at a wide angle (fork_stems 5, fork_angle 50, were 4 and 40), in iNaturalist photographs (observations 18299511, 185799293). Shorter shoots and sparser attraction points (internode 0.35, space_density 1.5, were 0.45 and 4) keep a crown of few thick limbs.

generator.params.pipe_rings.note: A choice of the model's (woody forms, broadleaf revision 16): wood laid down per m² of leaf a year, raised from 4e-5 so the water-storing trunk swells to about 1.6 m across at 100 years (it was 63 cm), as the bottle-shaped trunks in iNaturalist photographs do (observations 18299511, 185799293).

traits.crown_form.note: iNaturalist research-grade photographs (observations 18299511, 185799293, 37979372, 142536045): a few thick limbs spread from the top of the swollen trunk into a crown wider than tall.

traits.wood_density_basic_kg_m3.note: GWDD v.2.2 species aggregate for Adansonia digitata (gwddagg_v2.2_species.csv, read): specific gravity 0.31 (wsg_est, the database's hierarchical-model species mean, from 2 records in 1 source); trunks 0.3, branches 0.37. Basic density (oven-dry mass over green volume) is the specific gravity times 1000 kg/m3.

generator.params.path_half.note: A choice of the model's (crown form step B, broadleaf revision 11): the wood from the base at which a shoot's nodes are half as long, fitted so the plant grows to the height of its oldest reference size, with the crown's width left to grow inside the loose region.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a massive tree of the African savanna, 10 to 20 m tall, with a swollen, smooth grey bottle-shaped trunk storing water, a few thick, crooked branches high up and digitate leaves of five to seven leaflets, dropped in the dry season. Not fitted to measurements. space_kill 0.6 (was 1.0) since the growth-form language (revision 145): at 1.0 a young tree crowded its own buds to death in some seeds (seed 1 at 6 to 8 years, then 5.9 m at 100 years against 15 m); at 0.6 seeds 1 to 9 reach 12.4 to 15.5 m. Its crown's width is the broadleaf trees' rule from the measured width over height of open-grown trees of its lineage (crown_spread, USDA Urban Tree Database) since 2026-10-23, in place of a hand-set crown_radius. Its crown's base is the broadleaf trees' rule from the measured share of the tree's height below its crown (crown_base_share, USDA Urban Tree Database), and its stem divides only where its flora or photographs say its leader is lost or that it stands on several stems, since 2026-10-24, in place of hand-set crown_base and fork values.

allometry.note: Rough heights from general knowledge of the species: about 9 m at 40 years and 15 m at 100. Wide tolerances.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye from photographs: smooth grey bark, mid-green leaves. Bark pattern (plant roadmap P4, `bark_pattern`): smooth grey bark, mottled and folded; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).
